prediction: The report provides an overview of the Federal Bureau of Prisons' (BOP) use of retention incentives, internal controls, and strategic planning. Retention incentives are primarily funded through the Salaries and Expenses account and are subject to OPM regulations. BOP has internal controls in place to ensure the proper application, approval, and monitoring of retention incentives. These controls include a multi-layered review process involving the institution, regional office, and Central Office. BOP officials also conduct annual reviews to determine the continued necessity of retention incentives. Additionally, BOP has not evaluated the effectiveness of its retention incentives, which limits the ability to make data-driven decisions. The report recommends that BOP develop a strategic human capital plan and evaluate the effectiveness of retention incentives to better align with its human capital goals.
